analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Birla Fashion has posted net losses in 5 of the last 6 years, carries a complex demerger-driven revenue profile (INR 12,418 Cr in FY23 → INR 6,441 Cr in FY24 after spinning off Madura Brands), and has no clear path to sustained profitability. Without a 'what's the story?' answer I can explain simply, I don't invest.
key_strengths: Pantaloons and ethnic wear (Sabyasachi, Tasva) are genuine consumer brands with pricing power in the premiumising Indian fashion market
OCF has been positive in all 5 years (INR 644 Cr → 1,644 Cr), as EBITDA benefits from INDAS 116 lease capitalisation — showing underlying store-level economics are not terrible
Post-demerger balance sheet is cleaner: total debt down from INR 9,450 Cr (FY24) to INR 5,016 Cr (FY25), reducing financial risk
key_risks: Persistently loss-making at the net level (INR -736 Cr in FY24, -456 Cr in FY25) with negative ROE of -10.9% and negative ROCE of -2.87% — the business is destroying shareholder value
Revenue has effectively shrunk post-demerger with no clear timeline for the remaining entity (Pantaloons + ethnic) to reach profitability at scale
Finance costs have compounded at 18% CAGR since FY19 to INR 608 Cr in FY25 — interest is consuming most of whatever operating profit exists
red_flags: 6 consecutive years of near-net losses or actual losses since FY19 — this is not a turnaround story, this is a structural problem
EV/EBITDA of 197x is the most extreme valuation in this peer group and reflects how little true economic profit this business generates after leases and interest
Revenue trajectory is impossible to read cleanly due to demerger — the 6Y CAGR of -1.6% includes the full Madura business in prior years, making any growth projection speculative
analysis.detailed_analysis: ABFRL is exactly the kind of complicated, restructuring-heavy story Lynch avoids: multiple brand portfolios, demergers, rights issues, high debt, and persistent losses that obscure what the core business actually earns. The separation of the Madura lifestyle brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly) has dramatically shrunk reported revenues, and the remaining entity — Pantaloons + ethnic wear — has yet to prove standalone viability. The post-demerger balance sheet looks better (debt fell INR 4,400 Cr in FY25), but that came from equity raises, not earnings.
